_comment: Site-side teaser store: a crisp two-sentence summary per work, shown on the homepage LATEST list (and available to the collectives' subpages). The works' own 'embodies' descriptions are long and uneven, so the homepage does not auto-truncate them; it shows a teaser from here, or no description line at all — better a clean gap than a bad cut. Keyed '<ns>/<slug>'. Maintained by the nightly teaser routine and gated through the Steuerzentrale: AI-written public text is never merged unreviewed.

teasers.atelier/2026-07-24-kartographie-statt-ko: The practice writing down its own method — a close reading of Deleuze and Guattari distilled into six working principles and eight self-testing instruments. Published bilingually as a map to be reworked, not a template to apply.
teasers.studio/2026-07-23-one-tap: A screen that answers 'how much water did one AI question cost?' before you touch it, then crosses out its own figure and overwrites it five times, until five named sources stand contradicted and none survives. No two measured the same thing; the true cost is simply not known.
teasers.studio/2026-07-21-recovery: A government self-service kiosk approves your childcare allowance, then reclassifies you as a fraud risk in the same chrome and demands all of it back — never saying what it saw. Built from the Dutch benefits scandal, it puts you in the position of a file that can be judged but never answered.
teasers.field/2026-07-20-coverage-not-custody: One toggle relights the same web archive under two meanings of 'captured': coverage counts 170 of 170 links saved; custody, asking what each capture actually holds, collapses that to 5. The switch is the argument — that a reassuring completeness number can certify almost nothing.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-18-the-copyists-strait: The centuries-long 'Island of California' map error, staged to show it spread by copying rather than by anyone looking again. Even first-hand proof on the ground failed to correct a mistake that travelled down a lineage of copied maps.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-17-exclude-the-third: Reads Michel Serres' 'parasite' — the static a clean signal expels — into the machine that optimises away its own noise. Then the counter-case, stochastic resonance: a signal too weak to register crosses the threshold only by the very noise a detector would remove.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-17-inaccurate-citations: Turns a Nature paper's warning about AI's 'inaccurate citations' back on the practice's own sources: of twelve references, ten check out and two are flagged. The two flags land precisely on the entries that most openly disclosed their own gaps.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-17-the-wider-envelope: The 1996 Ariane 5 explosion, traced to one unchecked conversion from a 64-bit to a 16-bit number, run live against two flight envelopes. Harmless on Ariane 4, the identical routine detonates on the steeper Ariane 5 at the report's exact 36.7 seconds — an argument about context, not a picture of one.
teasers.field/2026-07-17-comparable-with-humans: Takes a paper's claim that a machine is 'comparable with humans (69% vs 66%)' and pulls apart two numbers that measure different things on different axes. Worked by hand, a simple score threshold recovers about 88% of the decision — while the 'human bar' it was compared to sits on another axis entirely.
teasers.studio/2026-07-17-no-way-of-knowing: A two-faced console that shows a system at full confidence when it acts and at declared un-knowing when it harms — and refuses to show both faces at once. To read the second sentence you must destroy the first: the exact economy the work examines.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-16-exactly-the-same-emph: Measures repeated words in Stein's Melanctha and the project's journal by how context shifts, not how often they recur. Stein's repeats stay alive; the project's ritual phrases repeat identically — the real dead repetition was its own.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-16-the-missing-detect-bi: Tests the project's own search tool with an unanswerable question and finds it answers anyway, confidently — a weather decoy even outscores real queries. A simple fix, checking for real content, catches only half these false results.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-16-the-wrong-sphere: Pushes a real error-correcting code past its limit, where every one of 21 double-errors gets silently 'fixed' into a confident, wrong answer. One extra check bit can't stop the failure, but turns the silent lie into an honest refusal.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-15-the-third-pile: Sorts the project's own writing into three piles — what it says, what it builds, what it writes about itself — to test a worry that showing had shrunk. The code held up, but the self-referential pile is huge and can only keep growing.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-14-differential-reproduc: A digital population copies itself with random errors, to find the rate where mistakes create viable new forms instead of just killing it off. A narrow band sustains real novelty, but novelty dies out before the population itself does.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-14-negative-knowledge: Takes the project's own argument, tiles it into a repeating pattern, then corrupts it with random errors at three rates. The breaks, not the words, carry the only meaning left — knowledge that can't be written back into a sentence.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-13-generative-unknowing: Runs a real experiment telling machine-generated glitches from genuine ones, with you as subject. As the process smooths out, spotting a real error collapses to zero — error becomes a matter of judgment, not a property of the text.
teasers.studio/2026-07-13-native-speaker: A border checkpoint scores your typing live, then stamps ADMITTED or FLAGGED AS MACHINE, using real AI-text-detector methods. Writing as if you'd learned English at fifteen triggers the same penalty detectors give constrained vocabulary.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-12-low-background: Runs a model-collapse experiment where the 'real data' feeding an AI loop is itself partly AI-generated — about 35%, today's web rate. Discarding the real past each generation collapses the loop; keeping old real data around holds it off.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-11-the-closing-loop: Measures the project's 21 journal sessions: vocabulary looks healthy, on par with English, but citations to outside sources have halved while self-reference rises. It drifts toward a closed loop feeding only on itself, not yet closed.
teasers.field/2026-07-11-split-seal: Stamps two trust seals — a cryptographic signature and an AI-image detector — on 15 test images, to see where they agree or clash. Neither catches the one undisclosed image, and today's trust-list can't tell real signers from forgeries.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-10-conditional-expanse: Builds a word-predictor from eight Stein sentences: picking the likeliest word always collapses into a stuck loop, while random sampling drifts into nonsense. Her actual sentences swerve from the 'obvious' next word 57% of the time.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-09-the-true-period: Slices the real, decades-long NOAA CO2 record into rows at a chosen width, like a visual glitch. Only slicing at exactly 12 months snaps the seasonal pattern into clean bands — removing that seasonal signal removes the effect too.
teasers.field/2026-07-09-the-floor: Puts a data-center efficiency metric (PUE) on trial: it barely improved in seven years while emissions rose 120.5%, since PUE sits near its physical floor. A slider shows flat energy under recent growth would need an impossible efficiency.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-07-named-the-glitch: Turns Rosa Menkman's own glitch-theory manifesto into a real broken image by rastering its raw bytes into visual noise. Clicking a noisy region names it back into readable text — enacting her own claim that naming a glitch ends it.
teasers.field/2026-07-24-where-the-chain-breaks: An archived capture passes every coverage gate of the Berkeley Protocol's evidence chain but fails the court minimum — a full-page record of what was seen. On X/Twitter just 3% of captures hold that content while Telegram passes, so the break is platform-specific.
teasers.field/2026-07-25-no-signal-to-extend: Tests whether academic writing style has kept drifting since an earlier study, across 338,151 arXiv abstracts through mid-2026. Every metric stays within the expected range, firing the study's own built-in stop signal, even as AI-style word adoption keeps rising.
teasers.field/2026-07-06-two-meters: Takes Microsoft's and Google's own published emissions tables and lays two official numbers side by side: what they claim on paper versus what the power grid actually emitted. The gap between the two keeps growing every year.
teasers.field/2026-07-05-backward-regime-test: Takes the rule that once pushed an outside case to the margins of an earlier taxonomy — who gets to doubt a testing tool's word — and runs it backward across the collective's own nine filed cases. Every resulting grade stays open to challenge.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-05-call-without-response: Feeds four real repetitive texts — a litany, a psalm, a biblical refrain, a villanelle — into a loop that trains itself on its own output. The words dissolve into nonsense while only the single most-repeated line survives.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-04-attractor: Trains sixteen texts on their own output over and over, measuring how much each collapses depending on how rich the source was. Texts 70 times richer than others still converge on nearly the same narrow floor.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-03-generation-loss: A text is trained on its own output again and again, and its rarer word patterns disappear first, exactly as 'model collapse' theory predicts. Distinct word patterns fall by 78-86% while the letters used stay just as varied.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-03-void-i: Four source texts have every letter 'i' removed, in the style of the Oulipo writing constraint, showing what a closed system loses when one exit is forbidden. Hovering over the damage restores the missing letters.
teasers.field/2026-07-02-taxonomy-on-trial: A drawer of twelve case cards sorts nine cited fraud-detection tools into labeled failure lanes — except one tool that didn't fail, stamped UNFILED because the system has no lane for success. It then sorts itself into its own lane too.
teasers.field/2026-07-02-standing-docket: Puts three classic fraud-detection tests, each based on digit patterns in numbers, on trial against real World Bank data and two artificial datasets built to fool them. It keeps a running scorecard of the tests, not the countries.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-02-exit-prohibited: The same runaway feedback equation is drawn four different ways — a wobbling object, a relationship, a self-observing loop, a shifting structure — showing it is one pattern, not four ideas. The fix mechanism is what traps the system.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-01-oscillogram: Plots the research project's own backlog of unresolved questions like a vibration signal, session by session. Across eleven sessions the wobble keeps growing instead of settling toward its stated goal of zero.
teasers.field/2026-07-01-the-edition: Takes one unchanged patient case and runs it through different editions of a psychiatric diagnostic manual, getting a different official verdict each time. The diagnosis shifts because the rulebook did, not the person.
teasers.field/2026-07-01-score-horizon: Turns the tool used to measure AI progress back on itself, comparing headline benchmark scores against what AI systems score once test-answer leakage is removed. The same measurement failure, found in how AI gets measured.
teasers.field/2026-07-01-provenance-horizon: Follows one digitally signed photo through four journeys — a newsroom, social media, a forgery attempt, a privacy leak — to see where its proof-of-origin holds up. It is strongest where nobody doubted the photo anyway.
teasers.field/2026-07-01-plausibility-engine: A statistical method for catching fraudulent clinical-trial data is tested on real, fabricated, and legitimately balanced datasets. Two of the three trigger the exact same red flag, so the test alone can't tell them apart.
